;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
***The [[Government of Mongolia|government]] announces the re-opening of retail stores, cultural and public events, production, and entertainment centers tomorrow, as well as schools, universities, and kindergartens on September 21. However, the country's borders will remain closed. [https://news.mn/en/793934/ (News.mn)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]] reports 1,113 deaths, the country's highest in two weeks, thus bringing the death toll to 133,119. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-brazil/brazil-registers-1113-coronavirus-deaths-highest-toll-in-almost-two-weeks-idUSS0N2FD01D (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[Canada–United States relations]]
**[[Canada–United States trade relations]], [[First Trump tariffs|Trump tariffs]]
***The United States announces the suspension of the 10 percent [[tariff]] imposed on [[Canada|Canadian]] [[aluminum]] imports since August with the [[Office of the U.S. Trade Representative]] citing a "sharp" decline in imports for the decision. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/wires/20200915-us-removes-10-percent-tariff-canadian-aluminum (AFP via RFI)]
*[[European migrant crisis]], [[Germany–Greece relations]]
**[[Germany]] agrees to take 1,500 migrants from [[Greece]] following a devastating fire at the [[Moria Refugee Camp]] on the island of [[Lesbos]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/09/15/germany-to-take-in-1-500-migrants-from-greek-islands-after-lesbos-fire (Euronews)] 
*Turkish [[Volkan Bozkır]] becomes the new [[President of the United Nations General Assembly]]. [https://news.un.org/en/story/2020/06/1066562 (UN News)]
;Law and crime
*[[Immigration detention in the United States]]
**A [[whistleblower]] working at an [[Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] facility in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] details a high rate of [[hysterectomies]] and other alleged medical neglect in a complaint to the [[Department of Homeland Security]]. Rep. [[Bennie Thompson]], the [[House Homeland Security Committee]] chairman, says the allegations of hysterectomies being performed on women without consent are "incredibly disturbing". [https://www.cnn.com/2020/09/15/politics/immigration-customs-enforcement-medical-care-detainees/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-54160638 (BBC News)]
*[[Poisoning of Alexei Navalny]]
**[[Russian opposition]] figure [[Alexei Navalny]] issues his first public statement since his poisoning via [[Instagram]], having been taken off the [[ventilator]] the previous day. [https://today.rtl.lu/news/world/a/1580244.html (AFP via RTL Today)]
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**A woman is killed in [[Cabo Delgado Province|Cabo Delgado]], [[Mozambique]], by [[Mozambique Defence Armed Forces|soldiers]] accusing her of being an [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]]-linked group militant. A soldier beat her with a stick several times before the rest of the group was ordered to "kill her on the side of the road" and shoot her. The [[murder]] is condemned by [[human rights in Mozambique|human rights]] groups, while authorities promise an investigation. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-54159307 (BBC News)] 
*[[Shooting of Breonna Taylor]]
**The city of [[Louisville, Kentucky]], settles a [[Wrongful death claim|wrongful death]] lawsuit with the family of Breonna Taylor, who was killed in a raid on her apartment by [[Louisville Metro Police Department|police]] in March. Her family will receive $12 million and several police reforms will also be enacted in the city as part of the agreement. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/09/15/us/breonna-taylor-louisville-settlement/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Lebanon Ohio Fifth Third Bank Robbery]]
**A [[bank robbery]] occurs at a [[Fifth Third Bank]] in [[Warren County, Ohio]]. [https://www.daytondailynews.com/news/warren-county-fifth-third-bank-held-up-in-robbery/XZ5FZY7WNZBJBCUBMMT5NH7ZNY/ (''Dayton Daily News'')]
